recipe: Beef brisket tagine with apricots, sultanas & almonds
servesNote: 2 portions — 895 kcal / 58 g protein each, and it doubles to 4 in the same pot. ⭐ This dish spends nine pantry items and buys six, which is why it earns its place.
adaptations: ⚠️ THE TOMATO PASTE AND ROASTED GARLIC PASTE SACHETS ARE NOT IN THE HOUSE — both recorded OUT on 3 Sep. Use 1 tbsp tomato double concentrate from the tube and 1 tbsp chopped garlic from the jar. Step 5 (frying the garlic in hot fat) and step 6 (frying the concentrate to brick) both still matter and do the mellowing.
⚠️ SULTANAS ARE DOWN TO 30 g, which is exactly what this recipe wants and leaves none. Check the tub before you commit — this is the only dish that would take the lot.
⚠️ RAS EL HANOUT IS NOT IN THIS DISH, but BAHARAT is, and the house holds one sachet. If it has gone: 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp pepper, ¼ tsp cayenne and a pinch of ginger stands in.

⛔ THE BRISKET AND THE APRICOTS ARE NOT IN THE HOUSE and were not on Tuesday's list. This is a shop-first dish. Buy the smallest Aldi brisket joint (~0.9 kg), trim it, and use the lot at double quantities — per-portion drops to ~£3.30 and hands-on barely moves.

⭐ CORNFLOUR IS OUT, so the step-12 shortcut for a thin sauce is unavailable. Reduce it properly instead: lift the meat with a slotted spoon and boil the liquid down. Brisket's collagen is largely insoluble and does NOT self-thicken its braising liquid the way chuck does, so expect to do this.

prep: ⭐ BLOOM THE SAFFRON FIRST, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. Crumble it into a cup with 3 tbsp hot — not boiling — water and leave it while you cook. Boiling water scalds the delicate aromatics; you want the liquid deep orange and smelling of honey and hay before it goes in. Saffron added dry to a braise contributes colour and almost nothing else.
Trim the hard waxy fat cap but LEAVE THE SOFT INTERNAL MARBLING ALONE — that marbling is the whole point of the cut. Cut across the grain into 4 cm chunks, pat dry, season.

steps.text: Oil in the casserole, medium-high, until it shimmers. Brown in TWO batches, single layer with space, until each has a deep even crust on at least two sides. Out to a plate. ⭐ Browning is not traditional Moroccan practice, but with a cut this lean-tasting on its own it is worth the ten minutes.

Medium heat. Onions and a good pinch of salt, stirring and scraping, until they have collapsed to about a third of their volume and turned soft and golden, with the browned meat residue lifted off the base. ⭐ This is the body of the sauce. Do not rush them.
Push aside. Chopped garlic, then baharat, ginger, cumin, turmeric and cinnamon straight into the hot fat, stirring constantly until fragrant and slightly darkened. ⚠️ Do not let them catch.
Tomato concentrate, fried until brick-coloured. Then HALF the harissa — hold the rest back for the end, when you can taste what you actually have.

Brisket and its juices back in. Saffron water — swill the cup out with a splash of stock so none is left behind — and enough stock that the liquid comes only about TWO-THIRDS up the meat. ⭐ A tagine is a braise that reduces to a thick clinging sauce, not a stew in broth.

Surface barely shivering, LID ON, oven at 150°C / 130°C fan, until a chunk gives way completely under a spoon with no springiness. Check halfway; a splash of hot water if the meat stands proud and dry.

Apricots and sultanas in, then back into the oven UNCOVERED until the fruit is plump and swollen and the sauce has reduced to a glossy coating that clings to the meat rather than a liquid it sits in. ⭐ The fruit goes in late on purpose — a full three hours and it dissolves entirely, taking its texture and most of its tartness with it.
Meanwhile toast the almonds in a dry pan, shaking often, until nutty and patchily golden. Straight out onto a plate — they carry on colouring and go from toasted to acrid very quickly.

⭐ Now balance it, OFF THE HEAT, tasting after each addition, and in this order: a good squeeze of LEMON FIRST (the correction that stops it tasting like a pudding), then SALT, then the remaining HARISSA if you want more heat, and only then the HONEY IF it needs sweetness. ⚠️ Most of the time, with apricots and sultanas already in, it will not.

Still thin? Lift the meat out with a slotted spoon and boil the liquid until it coats the back of a spoon, then return the meat. ⚠️ Expect to do this — brisket's collagen is largely insoluble and it does not thicken its own braising liquid the way chuck does.

Couscous: in a heatproof bowl with a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of oil, rubbed through with your fingers so the grains are coated. Pour over an equal volume of boiling stock or water (130 ml for 130 g), cover tightly and leave completely undisturbed 10 minutes. Then fluff with a FORK, never a spoon. Stirring it while it absorbs is what makes couscous clump.

Serve over the couscous, scattered with the toasted almonds and coriander, lemon wedges alongside. Maria's next-day lunch: reheat gently with a splash of water — the sauce sets solid when chilled and loosens back. ⛔ Keep the almonds and coriander separate; toasted almonds left in the sauce overnight go soft and there is nothing to be done about it. Couscous fresh each time.
